text:
William Nylander is in the middle of Toronto's storm. The Leafs are winless in seven, Jim Hiller has moved him to the third line, and the week's headlines have been Paul Bissonnette questioning his effort, Matthew Barnaby comparing him to Alexei Kovalev and Nate Thompson wondering if the writing is on the wall for him and Auston Matthews. Nylander's answer, per The Leafs Nation, is that he "doesn't feel he is cheating for offence."

The numbers say both sides have a point. He has 11 goals, but he's pointless in five and has four points in his last 10, and our form check finds some of each: fewer chances (11.1 on-ice expected goals against 13.7 usual) and finishing that dried up. Toronto has only 41.5% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, almost eight points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey flagged the defensive cost last season too (bottom 6% of forwards), even as it rated him 34th of 401 overall.

His top shot, 99.3 mph, still sits at the very top of the league on NHL EDGE. The question is whether he gets back to places where it matters.
